description.narrative: The proposed project will support the Government of Solomon Islands to improve tax administration. The development outcome will be improved domestic resource mobilization. This outcome will be achieved through (i) more efficient tax administration that provides better services to taxpayers; and (ii) increased capacity of the Inland Revenue Division (IRD) to manage the transition to a more efficient, fairer, and transparent tax framework. The project will assist in restructuring the IRD to (i) move to a functional structure and train staff in their new roles and processes, (ii) finance the acquisition of a new tax administration information system (TAIS) and train staff in its use, and (iii) deliver a public outreach program to increase taxpayer compliance.

description.narrative: Tax revenues increase annually at the rate of nominal gross domestic product growth or higher. Progress/Status: Revenue administration and project management support consulting firm hird on 24 March 2022, and the contract was awarded to Supply, Installation, Commissioning, and Maintenance of Tax Administration Information System (TAIS) on 22 July 2022. Data Source: a. Annual tax reports prepared by IRD (using International Monetary Fund gross domestic product estimates). Baseline value: TBD
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: A new fit-for-purpose TAIS acquired, and tax administration staff trained on how to obtain the greatest benefit from its use Indicator: At least 90% of TAIS users received training and reported increased skills on using the TAIS by 2027 (2020 baseline: 41 women and 66 men TAIS users; 0% trained) Progress/Status: Training of end-users started in June 2024 and will continue until the conclusion of the project. Additional training is being provided to specific end-users and system administrators following Phase 2 by AARC-C2D's new RMS Training specialist. Part 1 RMS Training in September 20025 was very well received by SIIRD RMS Users (110+ Users) and provides a foundation for subsequent RMS training for targeted RMS user teams/roles (66+ Users) which was delivered in November 2025. The newly established computer training lab has been a significant asset for training and collaborative sessions. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports Actual value:

Output: IRD capacity for gender-responsive and effective tax education and taxpayer services improved. Indicator: At least 200 women micro and small entrepreneurs received education/information sessions on tax rights and obligations by 2027. Progress/Status: This work will be guided and assisted by the taxpayer service and education improvement strategies, with gender considerations applied. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring report Actual value:

Output: IRD capacity for gender-responsive and effective tax education and taxpayer services improved. Indicator: At least 50% of the taxpayers required to remit VAT have at least one representative participate in one or more public information events by 2027 (2020 baseline: 0%) Progress/Status: While VAT Bill was sent to Parliament before the 2024 General Election it was required to be reconsidered and resubmitted to Parliament. The Bill is scheduled to be presented to Parliament in the first Parliamentary sitting of 2026. Government has asked for no public education on VAT ahead of the legislation being passed. The earliest start date for VAT is now 1 January 2028. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring report Actual value:

Output: IRD capacity for gender-responsive and effective tax education and taxpayer services improved. Indicator: At least 80% of the business assigned to the large taxpayer office who participated in education/information session on new VAT obligations/compliance requirements reported increased understanding by 2027 (2020 baseline: 0%) Progress/Status: Development of a taxpayer service and education strategy, incorporating LTO, was approved in Q2 of 2024. Delays have occurred due to other priorities namely the RMS upgrade. The VAT Bill is scheduled to be presented to Parliament in the first Parliamentary sitting of 2026. Government has asked for no public education on VAT ahead of the legislation being passed. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring report Actual value:

Output: IRD capacity for gender-responsive and effective tax education and taxpayer services improved. Indicator: At least 80% of women who participated in education/information sessions on the new VAT obligations/compliance requirements, and reported increased understandings by 2027 (2020 baseline: 0%) Progress/Status: When education/information sessions are delivered, we will pose a question to taxpayers to assess whether their knowledge/skills increased, with results to be disaggregated by gender. The VAT Bill is scheduled to be presented to Parliament in the first Parliamentary sitting of 2026. Government has asked for no public education on VAT ahead of the legislation being passed. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring report Actual value:

Output: IRD capacity for gender-responsive and effective tax education and taxpayer services improved. Indicator: Sex-disaggregated taxpayer end line survey taken during the second half of the project shows at least 10% increase (compared to the baseline taxpayer survey taken during the first half of the project) among men and women taxpayers who rate their experience with the IRD as satisfactory or better (2023 baseline: 32 women and 46 men of the 111 respondents [43 women, 68 men] rated their overall experience with IRD staff as satisfactory or better) Progress/Status: Survey results reported in the third Quarter of 2023 have been used to inform the taxpayer services improvement plan. This was approved in Q2 of 2024.In addition, following the endline survey, an assessment will be conducted to determine whether there has been an increase in satisfaction levels with IRD services (overall and by gender). Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring report Actual value:

Output: Tax administration restructured along functional lines, and staff trained in new roles and business processes Indicator: At least 90% of IRD senior staff received training on how to integrate gender considerations when designing new policies, programs, services, and initiatives and reported increased skills by 2027 (2020 baseline: 20 senior officers [5 women, 15 men] 0 trained) Progress/Status: Work has not yet begun. A preliminary reflection tool has been developed (included in the Q3 report updated that could be used to assess the gender impacts of IRD policies and programs. However, due to capacity issues, it was agreed that ADB would provide a resource to develop and deliver this training. Discussions and planning with ADB to be pursued in 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports. Actual value:

Output: Tax administration restructured along functional lines, and staff trained in new roles and business processes Indicator: At least 90% of IRD staff (49 women, 68 men) trained in gender equality, social inclusion, and reported increased understanding by 2027 (2020 baseline: 49 women, 68 men, 0 trained). Progress/Status: This work will be guided and assisted by the IRD GAP. Based on discussions with central agency partners, there is no stand-alone training on gender equality, however elements are included in the “Knowing Your Public Service course” which is mandatory for onboarding and induction and required for promotions and offered only twice a year. An introduction to gender equality induction has been developed and delivered to IRD Champions, another workshop developed and delivered to IRD Executive Team, and a series of GE info sessions were delivered to team leaders and employees. To date 104 of 130 employees. (80% of staff) have participated at these information sessions) - 46 (or 44%) were men and 58 (or 56%) were women. Additional information sessions will be held in 2026 to ensure that all staff receive the information. Material for the course has been updated, and a supplementary facilitator guide has been developed that will be used by GE Champions to deliver the info sessions. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports. Actual value:

Output: Tax administration restructured along functional lines, and staff trained in new roles and business processes Indicator: At least 90% of IRD staff received training and reported increased skills in business processes by 2027 (2020 baseline: 49 women; 68 men) Progress/Status: Business process advisor has assisted in numerous meetings and brainstorming sessions on business processes, covering a range of topics, including registration, new-taxpayer education, incident management, dishonoured cheques, unidentified payments debt collection, non-filing enforcement, as well as components of processes (e.g., issuing garnishee notices to collect debts, imposing penalties at the end of an audit). Advising on the establishment and implementation of new SIIRD Process Development and Quality Assurance roles - including frameworks, tools and capability
A small debt reduction forum to discuss debt reduction strategies and processes was also formed, and represented by the Commissioner, both Deputy Commissioners, two Assistant Deputy Commissioners, a team leader, and four project advisers. Of the 10 members, one is a woman (10%). Statistics are kept on attendance at all training and evaluations are completed on collusion of each session to identify increased skills. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports. Actual value:

Output: Tax administration restructured along functional lines, and staff trained in new roles and business processes Indicator: At least 90% of IRD women senior staff access new training or coaching on management and/or leadership, and reported increased skills by 2027 (2020 baseline: 20 senior officers [5 women, 15 men]; 0 trained or coached) Progress/Status: A management development program (targeting team leaders and above) was developed in 2024, and roll-out commenced in March 2025. All IRD senior female staff (comprising ten women) participated in this program. In addition, two employees (both women) were nominated to participate in IPAM's mentorship program and leadership development program. A subsequent series of recap sessions on Module 1 was held in December and all managers attended, except those on provincial visits and annual leave. In total, there were 23 attendants—14 men and 9 women. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports. Actual value:

Output: A new fit-for-purpose TAIS acquired, and tax administration staff trained on how to obtain the greatest benefit from its use Indicator: Upgraded TAIS tested and fully operational by 2026 (2020 baseline: Previous version of TAIS that limits IRD's functions) Progress/Status: Phase 1 of system upgrade has gone live as of 22 July 2024. This includes all tax administration core functionalities such as registration, cashier, assessment, audit, collection, objection and refunds. Some issues are still being identified and are progressively being fixed. Development/configuration of VAT is incomplete, but the tax will be applicable only from January 2027 at the earliest.
Agreement on the scope of Phase 2, was signed off by both parties on 3 April 2025. The system should be fully operational by the end of May 2026 almost 9 months behind schedule. External interfaces with third parties will not occur in the way intended. A manual process will be developed.
There are several fundamental elements of RMS Z which have not worked since deployment (July 2024) and have a Sev1 status. There are also numerous other bugs of varying severity.
There remain question marks around DTL's resourcing model - and whether there are sufficient resources (& the right ones) being applied to IRD's Sev1/2, bugs and change items. A modest UAT Release was deployed on 15th December 2025 - with Revised Income Tax Returns, some Sev1 and other item fixes. Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: A new fit-for-purpose TAIS acquired, and tax administration staff trained on how to obtain the greatest benefit from its use Indicator: Upgraded TAIS that collects sex-disaggregated data for gender-sensitive tax analysis installed by 2025 (2020 baseline: Upgraded TAIS not installed) Progress/Status: Phase 1 of system upgrade went live on 22 July 2024. Enhancements to the Business Intelligence database along with several new RMS Reports will be implemented as part of Phase 2. This will enable more flexible reporting. Sex-disaggregated data has been built into the system. Agreement on the scope of Phase 2, including the above, was signed off by both parties on 3 April 2025. Further Phase 2 items were deployed into production in late August 2025, with other items remaining to be delivered Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: IRD capacity for gender-responsive and effective tax education and taxpayer services improved. Indicator: Gender-responsive public information campaign on tax system, including VAT, developed and implemented by 2027 (2020 baseline: No gender-responsive information campaign). Progress/Status: This work will be guided and assisted by the taxpayer service and education improvement strategies, with gender considerations applied. Preliminary information sessions have begun, with the VAT advisor providing information on how to calculate the transitional VAT input tax credit on the first VAT return during an information session to Chamber of Commerce and Industry on September 23, 2024. Government has asked for no public education on VAT ahead of the legislation being passed. This has seriously limited the project's ability to implement VAT. The Bill is scheduled to be presented to Parliament in the first Parliamentary sitting of 2026.
Data Source: Quarterly project monitoring report Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y
